{
  "root_cause": "The component removes the maxlength attribute from the wrapper div instead of the textarea, leaving the hard limit in place and causing input to be truncated at 30 characters.",
  "repair_strategy": "Change the line that removes the maxlength attribute to target the textarea element ($textarea) rather than the container ($module).",
  "edits": [
    {
      "path": "src/govuk/components/character-count/character-count.js",
      "sha256": "b17688138faafe0e8e1b3b435f890c52c8dc6ca9fbcbb8644f2e93a5125f7b90",
      "before": "  // Remove hard limit if set\n  $module.removeAttribute('maxlength')",
      "after": "  // Remove hard limit if set\n  $textarea.removeAttribute('maxlength')"
    }
  ],
  "expected_accessibility_effect": "Users can exceed the limit and receive accurate character count feedback, with error messages and live region updates reflecting the true state, ensuring conformance with WCAG 2.1.1, 2.4.3, and 4.1.2.",
  "functional_risks": [
    "Unlikely regression as only the textarea's maxlength affects input limitation; the wrapper's attribute is unused.",
    "Potential impact if other code erroneously relied on the wrapper's maxlength attribute (none identified).",
    "Ensuring noscript fallback retains the maxlength attribute for users without JavaScript."
  ],
  "verification_requirements": [
    "After initialization, the textarea must have no maxlength attribute.",
    "Typing more than 30 characters retains the full input and the counter shows negative remaining characters (e.g., 'You have 4 characters too many').",
    "Error styling (govuk-textarea--error, govuk-error-message) applies when over limit.",
    "Screen‑reader live region updates politely with the count message on each change.",
    "With JavaScript disabled, the hard limit still enforces the 30‑character maximum."
  ]
}

So the textarea's value ended up truncated.

There's also checkIfValueChanged called on focus interval to detect changes from speech recognition etc. It compares oldValue and if changed, updates count message but does not modify value. Thus the bug: The component should remove the maxlength attribute from the textarea, not just the wrapper. According to comment: "A hard maxlength is kept for users without JavaScript; the character count is meant to lift it." Means they intend to remove the maxlength via JS when JS is available, to allow exceeding limit and show character count messages. But they incorrectly removed from wrapper instead of textarea.

Root cause: The component incorrectly removes the maxlength attribute from the wrapper div instead of the textarea, leaving the hard limit in place and causing truncation of input beyond 30 characters.

Repair strategy: Change the line that removes the maxlength attribute to target the textarea element ($textarea) rather than the container ($module).
